description.narrative: Since January 2025, Burundi has received nearly 70,000 refugees from the Democratic Republic of Congo, mainly through Cibitoke province. Many are temporarily housed in overcrowded, inadequate facilities near the border, facing risks of malnutrition, disease, and mental health issues due to prior extreme violence. The Burundian government has granted refugee status and is working on relocation to camps. Existing national capacities are limited, as Burundi also hosts around 90,000 other asylum seekers and returnees. The UNHCR has declared the situation a Level 2 emergency, with coordination led by national authorities and UN agencies. Mental health services are provided in camps by HealthNet TPO and in temporary sites by Doctors Without Borders (MSF), the World Health Organization (WHO), and other non-gouvernmental organisations (NGOs), though no specific mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) emergency coordination structure exists yet.The objective of this initiative is to establish a coordination mechanism among key stakeholders, ensure better integration of MHPSS approaches within national public health and humanitarian policies, and support the development of standards and operating procedures tailored to the Ivorian context. Through this support, the project partners also aim to foster experience sharing, strengthen capacity-building efforts, and improve monitoring and evaluation mechanisms for MHPSS interventions.
